title: The station clock
intro: Each question is a separate puzzle.

All questions use an ordinary analog clock with a 12-hour dial and hour and minute hands, both moving smoothly (the minute hand turns 6 degrees a minute, the hour hand 0.5 degrees a minute). "The angle between the hands" is the smaller angle, from 0 to 180 degrees. A faulty clock runs at a steady, wrong rate.

questions.stem: How many times do the hands of a correct clock make a right angle (exactly 90 degrees) between 12:00 noon and 12:00 midnight? The hands are not at a right angle at either end.
why: The minute hand gains 5.5 degrees a minute on the hour hand, so the gap goes round 360 degrees every 720/11 minutes: 11 times in 12 hours.
Each round passes 90 and 270 degrees, both right angles: 11 x 2 = 22.

fig.note: A gap of 270 degrees one way is 90 the other: a right angle too.

questions.stem: What is the angle between the hands at 8:24, in degrees?
why: Hour hand: 8 x 30 + 24 x 0.5 = 252 degrees. Minute hand: 24 x 6 = 144 degrees.
252 - 144 = 108, already under 180.

questions.stem: At what time between 4 o'clock and 5 o'clock are the hands of a correct clock exactly opposite each other (180 degrees apart)?
why: At m minutes past 4 the hour hand is at 120 + 0.5m and the minute hand at 6m. Opposite: 6m - (120 + 0.5m) = 180, so 5.5m = 300.

questions.stem: Between 2:00 and 3:00 the angle between the hands is exactly 33 degrees at two different moments. How many minutes pass between these two moments?
why: At m minutes past 2 the gap is |60 - 5.5m|. Setting it to 33: 5.5m = 27 or 5.5m = 93, so m = 54/11 or 186/11.
The difference is 132/11 = 12 minutes.

questions.stem: A clock gains 5 minutes every hour of true time. It was set right at 8:00 AM. Later the same day the clock shows 9:00 PM. How many minutes of true time have passed since 8:00 AM?
why: The clock shows 65 minutes for every 60 true minutes. It has moved 13 hours = 780 clock minutes.
780 x 60/65 = 720 true minutes.

fig.note: Both started at 8:00; the clock ran 65 minutes for every 60.

steps: Measure from 12 in degrees: the minute hand moves 6 a minute, the hour hand 0.5, so the minute hand gains 5.5 degrees a minute.
For a time between h and h + 1 o'clock, the hour hand is at 30h + 0.5m and the minute hand at 6m; set the gap equal to the angle (or 360 minus it) and solve for m.
For counting, the gap goes round once every 720/11 minutes, 11 times in 12 hours; most angles happen twice a round.
For a faulty clock, measure from when it was right: clock time passed over true time passed is its rate (65/60 for one gaining 5 minutes an hour).

title: Mirrors, drifting clocks and counting
intro: Each question is a separate puzzle.

All questions use an ordinary analog clock with a 12-hour dial and hour and minute hands, both moving smoothly (the minute hand turns 6 degrees a minute, the hour hand 0.5 degrees a minute). "The angle between the hands" is the smaller angle, from 0 to 180 degrees. A faulty clock runs at a steady, wrong rate. In the mirror question the clock is seen in a flat mirror beside it: left and right swap, up and down do not.

questions.stem: A wall clock is seen in a flat vertical mirror, and the image shows the time 8:20. What is the actual time?
why: A mirror swaps left and right, so the image shows 12:00 minus the actual time.

fig.note: A mirror swaps left and right: the two times add up to 12:00.

questions.stem: Two clocks are set right together at noon on a Monday. One gains 3 minutes every hour; the other loses 2 minutes every hour. How many hours later do the two clocks next show the same time on their 12-hour dials?
why: They drift apart by 3 + 2 = 5 minutes an hour.
A 12-hour dial repeats after 720 minutes, so they agree again after 720/5 = 144 hours.

questions.stem: How many times are the hands of a correct clock exactly opposite each other (180 degrees apart) between 3:00 PM and 9:00 PM, counting 3:00 PM and 9:00 PM themselves if they qualify?
why: The hands are opposite every 720/11 minutes: in this stretch at 3:49 1/11, 4:54 6/11, 6:00, 7:05 5/11 and 8:10 10/11.
At 3:00 and 9:00 they are at 90 degrees, so neither end counts: 5.

questions.stem: Starting at 12:00 noon, the hands of a correct clock form a right angle for the 15th time (12:00 itself is not counted). How many minutes after noon is that, to the nearest whole minute?
why: Right angles come when 5.5t = 90 + 180k for k = 0, 1, 2 and so on; the 15th has k = 14.
t = 2610/5.5 = 474.55 minutes, which rounds to 475.

fig.note: The first right angle, then the 15th.

questions.stem: A watch that gains time at a steady rate is 2 minutes slow at noon on a Sunday and 4 minutes 48 seconds fast at 2:00 PM on the following Sunday. After how many hours from noon on the first Sunday was it correct?
why: The interval is 7 days 2 hours = 170 hours, in which the watch gains 2 min + 4 min 48 s = 408 seconds.
It was right once it had gained the first 120 seconds: 120/408 x 170 = 50 hours.

steps: Mirror: actual time = 12:00 minus the time in the mirror (add 12 hours first if the mirror shows between 12:00 and 1:00).
Two clocks drifting in opposite directions: add the drifts. They agree again when the gap reaches 12 hours, not 24.
For "how many times", list the moments from the first one, 720/11 minutes apart for opposite or coinciding hands, 360/11 apart for right angles, and check both ends.
A steadily gaining watch's error grows in proportion to time: find when it reaches zero by proportion.

title: Calendars
intro: Each question is a separate puzzle.

Use the Gregorian calendar: a year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, except that a year divisible by 100 is a leap year only if it is also divisible by 400. A week runs Monday to Sunday, and February has 28 days, or 29 in a leap year.

questions.stem: How many times does the 13th of a month fall on a Friday in the 28 years from 2001 to 2028, both years included?
why: The 13th is a Friday exactly when the 1st is a Sunday (12 days later is 5 weekdays on).
Counting the months that begin on a Sunday, year by year, from 2001 to 2028 gives 48.

questions.stem: The calendar of 2026 (the weekday of every date) repeats exactly in a later year. What is the first later year with the same calendar as 2026?
why: The year must also be non-leap and start on the same weekday. 2026 starts on a Thursday; each year moves the start on by 1 day, or 2 after a leap year.
Starts: 2027 Fri, 2028 Sat, 2029 Mon, 2030 Tue, 2031 Wed, 2032 Thu (but leap), 2033 Sat, 2034 Sun, 2035 Mon, 2036 Tue, 2037 Thu. The first match is 2037.

questions.stem: A non-leap year has exactly 53 Mondays. What day of the week is 25 December of that year?
why: A non-leap year is 52 weeks and 1 day, so only the weekday of 1 January comes 53 times: 1 January is a Monday, and so is 31 December (364 days later).
25 December is 6 days earlier: Tuesday.

questions.stem: 1 January 2000 was a Saturday. On which day of the week did 10 March 1812 fall?
why: 10 March 2000 is 69 days after 1 January 2000 (2000 is leap): 69 mod 7 = 6, so a Friday.
From 10 March 1812 to 10 March 2000: 188 x 365 + 46 leap days (1816 to 2000, without 1900) = 68,666 days, and 68,666 mod 7 = 3. Three weekdays before Friday is Tuesday.

questions.stem: In how many months of 2026 are there five Fridays, five Saturdays and five Sundays?
why: Only a 31-day month has three weekdays five times: those of its 1st, 2nd and 3rd. So the month must start on a Friday.
The 31-day months of 2026 start on Thu, Sun, Fri (May), Wed, Sat, Thu and Tue. Only May: 1.

fig.note: May 2026: it starts on a Friday, so Friday, Saturday and Sunday each come five times.

steps: A date d falls (d - 1) mod 7 weekdays after the 1st of its month, so the 13th is a Friday when the 1st is a Sunday.
A non-leap year moves the next year's first weekday on by 1 (365 = 52 weeks + 1); a leap year by 2. Two years share a calendar when both are leap or both are not, and they start on the same weekday.
Across many years, count the days between two dates (365 a year, plus each 29 February, none for century years not divisible by 400) and take the remainder by 7.
In a 31-day month the 29th, 30th and 31st fall on the same weekdays as the 1st, 2nd and 3rd, so those three weekdays come five times.

diagram.note: Each year's first weekday and whether it is a leap year: the run that finds 2026's twin.
